metadata.course: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: A quantitative introduction to astrophysics: astronomical measurement and the celestial sphere, gravitation and orbits, radiation and spectra, telescopes and detectors, binary stars and the HR diagram, stellar atmospheres and interiors, star formation and evolution, compact objects, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology, and the solar system with its exoplanets.

id_namespace.reason: Concept ids are global; the prefix keeps this course disjoint from the shipped courses that share concept titles.

textbook_alignment.link_only_note: OpenStax Astronomy 2e reports CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is carried as a link-only study reference: never stored, quoted or used as an anchor.

The Celestial Sphere, Coordinates & Time: Time Systems, Precession, Proper Motion & Parallax

Gravity, Orbits & Celestial Mechanics: Kepler's Laws & the Geometry of the Ellipse
The Two-Body Problem, Barycentre & Reduced Mass
Tides, the Roche Limit & Lagrange Points

Stellar Atmospheres & Interiors: The Radiation Field: Intensity, Flux & Radiation Pressure
Opacity, Mean Free Path & Optical Depth
Radiative Transfer, the Gray Atmosphere & Line Formation
Hydrostatic Equilibrium & the Equation of State
Stellar Structure Equations, the Virial Theorem & Timescales
The Sun as the Calibrating Standard Model

Cosmology & the Early Universe: Scale Factor, Critical Density & the Fate of the Universe
Inflation & the Horizon and Flatness Problems

The Solar System & Exoplanets: Minor Bodies of the Solar System

concepts.title: Absolute Magnitude and the Distance Modulus
concepts.summary: Apparent and absolute magnitude differ by m - M = 5 log10(d) - 5 with d in parsecs, so a star of absolute magnitude 0 placed at 100 pc has m = 5.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Accretion Discs and the Eddington Limit
concepts.summary: Accretion liberates GM(dM/dt)/R, so a neutron star accreting 10^-8 solar masses per year radiates about 10^31 W, and the Eddington limit caps how fast a compact object can be fed.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Angular Size and the Small-Angle Relation
concepts.summary: A body of diameter D at distance d subtends about D/d radians, so the Moon's 3 475 km at 384 000 km gives 0.52 degrees, and one angular size can mean a small near object or a large distant one.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Asteroids, Comets and the Kuiper Belt
concepts.topic: Minor Bodies of the Solar System
concepts.summary: Main-belt asteroids orbit between 2.2 and 3.3 au, comets arrive from the Kuiper belt and Oort cloud and grow tails only inside about 5 au, and the belt's total mass is under a thousandth of Earth's.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Atmospheric Windows and Space Observatories
concepts.summary: The atmosphere passes visible light and part of the radio band but absorbs ultraviolet, X-rays and most infrared, so those bands need balloons, rockets or space telescopes above most of the absorbing column.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Axes, Loci and the Main Sequence
concepts.summary: The HR diagram plots luminosity against temperature, and stars gather on a main sequence from hot and bright to cool and faint, with giants, supergiants and white dwarfs lying off it.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Barycentre and Reduced Mass
concepts.topic: The Two-Body Problem, Barycentre & Reduced Mass
concepts.summary: Two bodies circle their common centre of mass with m1 r1 = m2 r2, and the relative motion is one body of reduced mass m1 m2/(m1 + m2) orbiting the total mass, so a star with a planet wobbles by only m_p/M_star of the separation.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis and the Light Elements
concepts.summary: Within the first few minutes, as kT fell below about 1 MeV, nucleosynthesis left roughly 75 per cent hydrogen, 25 per cent helium-4 and traces of deuterium and lithium-7, which fixes the baryon-to-photon ratio.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Cepheids as Standard Candles
concepts.summary: The period-luminosity law makes a Cepheid a standard candle, so a ten-day Cepheid near 3x10^3 solar luminosities has its distance fixed by its period and apparent brightness to a few per cent.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Clusters, Groups and the Cosmic Web
concepts.summary: A galaxy cluster holds 10^2 to 10^3 galaxies within a few Mpc and is dominated by 10^7 to 10^8 K intracluster gas and dark matter, and clusters trace the filaments and voids of the cosmic web.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Collecting Area and Limiting Magnitude
concepts.summary: Collecting area grows as D^2, so a 0.2 m telescope gathers about 800 times the light of a 7 mm dark-adapted pupil, worth roughly 7 magnitudes of extra reach.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Colour Index and Bolometric Correction
concepts.summary: The difference of two band magnitudes is a temperature proxy, B - V near 0.65 for the Sun and negative for a hot B star, and the bolometric correction turns a band magnitude into total flux, mattering most at both temperature extremes.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Colour-Magnitude Diagrams of Star Clusters
concepts.summary: Replacing temperature by colour index and luminosity by absolute magnitude gives the observed colour-magnitude diagram, whose turnoff fixes a cluster's age and whose red-giant branch tracks its metallicity.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Comparative Geology of the Terrestrial Planets
concepts.summary: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars share a rocky differentiated composition but differ in atmosphere and surface because planet size sets whether gas is retained and whether plate tectonics or volcanism dominates.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Conservation of Angular Momentum
concepts.summary: Specific angular momentum h = r v cos(phi) is constant because gravity is a central force, which is why a comet is fastest at perihelion and why dA/dt = h/2 never changes.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Core-Collapse and Thermonuclear Supernovae
concepts.summary: A star above about eight solar masses ends in a core-collapse supernova that releases near 10^46 J and leaves a neutron star or black hole, while a Type Ia comes from a white dwarf reaching 1.4 solar masses and is standardisable for cosmology.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Cosmological Redshift and the Scale Factor
concepts.summary: Cosmological redshift obeys 1 + z = a_observed/a_emitted, so z = 1 means the light left when the universe was half its present size.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Dark Energy and the Equation of State
concepts.summary: Dark energy supplies about 68 per cent of the energy budget with an equation of state w = p/(rho c^2) consistent with -1, which is why the expansion accelerates although gravity pulls inward.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Detectors, Integration Time and Signal-to-Noise
concepts.summary: A CCD accumulates signal linearly while read noise and sky background add in quadrature, so signal-to-noise grows as sqrt(t) when background-limited but only as t when read-noise-limited.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Dimensional Analysis of Physical Laws
concepts.summary: An equation is dimensionally consistent only when both sides carry the same base-unit powers, so a candidate such as L ~ M R^2/t^3 can be tested before any data are taken, though consistency alone does not prove a law correct.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Diurnal Rotation and Circumpolar Stars
concepts.summary: The sky turns once on the polar axis in a sidereal day, so a star of declination d culminates at altitude 90 - |latitude - d| degrees and never sets when d > 90 - latitude.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Doppler Shift and Radial Velocity
concepts.summary: For speeds well below c the shift is delta lambda/lambda = v_r/c, so a line at 500 nm displaced by 0.05 nm means 30 km/s, and only the line-of-sight component can be measured this way.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Equivalent Width and the Curve of Growth
concepts.summary: Line strength grows with the absorbing column in three regimes, linear in N, roughly as sqrt(ln N) in the Doppler core and as sqrt(N) on the damping wings, so equivalent width alone gives no abundance without the regime.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Flux, Luminosity and the Inverse-Square Law
concepts.summary: Flux falls as F = L/(4 pi d^2), so a star ten times farther away is a hundred times fainter, and a measured flux with a known distance yields the luminosity.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Focal Length, Magnification and Focal Ratio
concepts.summary: Angular magnification is f_objective/f_eye, and the focal ratio f/D fixes both the plate scale and the light concentration, so a 0.2 m f/10 telescope has a 2 m focal length.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Four Ways to Detect a Binary
concepts.summary: A binary is classed by how it is found, resolved visually, by periodic line splitting, by eclipses in the light curve or by the wobble of the primary, and each class yields a different mix of orbital parameters.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Gravitational Potential Energy and Escape Speed
concepts.summary: With U = -G M m / r measured from infinity, a body escapes when its kinetic energy balances the well, giving v_esc = sqrt(2GM/r), which is 11.2 km/s at Earth's surface.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Great Circles and Spherical Angles
concepts.summary: Two great circles cross at antipodal points and enclose an angle equal to the dihedral angle of their planes, while a small circle such as a declination parallel does not pass through the centre of the sphere.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Hierarchical Assembly in a Dark Matter Universe
concepts.summary: Structure grows bottom-up through mergers in a cold dark matter universe, so large galaxies are assembled from smaller pieces and their star formation peaks near redshift 2.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Horizon, Equatorial and Ecliptic Frames
concepts.summary: Each frame is tied to a different reference, the observer's zenith, Earth's equator or the ecliptic, so a star's altitude changes hourly while its right ascension and declination stay nearly fixed.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Hubble's Law and the Hubble Constant
concepts.summary: Recession grows with distance as v = H0 d, so H0 near 70 km/s/Mpc puts a galaxy at 100 Mpc at 7 000 km/s and gives a Hubble time of about 14 Gyr.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium and Central Conditions
concepts.topic: Hydrostatic Equilibrium & the Equation of State
concepts.summary: Each layer balances pressure against weight, dP/dr = -G M_r rho/r^2, which for the Sun implies a central pressure near 10^16 Pa and a central temperature near 1.5x10^7 K.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Individual Masses from the Barycentre
concepts.summary: The barycentre divides the orbit in the ratio of the masses, so the measured semi-major axes give M1/M2 = a2/a1 and, with the sum, each mass separately.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Inflation and the Horizon and Flatness Problems
concepts.topic: Inflation & the Horizon and Flatness Problems
concepts.summary: An epoch of exponential expansion by at least e^60 explains how causally disconnected patches share one background temperature and why Omega is driven so close to 1.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Kepler's Laws and Orbital Geometry
concepts.topic: Kepler's Laws & the Geometry of the Ellipse
concepts.summary: Orbits are ellipses with the primary at a focus, the radius vector sweeps equal areas in equal times, and P^2 = a^3 holds when P is in years and a in astronomical units.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Kirchhoff's Three Spectral Laws
concepts.summary: A hot dense body emits a continuum, a hot low-density gas emits bright lines at its own wavelengths, and a cooler gas in front of a continuum removes those same wavelengths as absorption lines.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Limb Darkening in a Gray Atmosphere
concepts.topic: Radiative Transfer, the Gray Atmosphere & Line Formation
concepts.summary: A grazing ray reaches optical depth 1 in a cooler, higher layer, so the solar disc darkens towards the limb, and the Eddington grey atmosphere predicts I(mu)/I(1) = (2 + 3 mu)/5 for mu = cos(theta).

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Logarithmic Plots and Power-Law Fits
concepts.summary: Plotting log y against log x turns y = k x^n into a straight line of slope n, which is how a luminosity-mass exponent near 3.5 is read straight off the graph.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Main-Sequence Lifetimes
concepts.summary: A star burns core hydrogen for about 10^10 (M/M_sun)^(-2.5) years, so a ten solar mass star lasts 3x10^7 years and a half-solar-mass star about 6x10^10 years.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Mass and Evolution Read off the HR Diagram
concepts.summary: Position on the main sequence fixes mass, so its upper end holds short-lived massive stars, and displacement off the sequence marks a post-main-sequence stage.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Neutron Star Structure and the Pulsar Beam
concepts.summary: A neutron star puts 1.4 solar masses inside a 10 km radius at nuclear density near 10^17 kg/m^3, and a misaligned magnetic dipole beams radiation that sweeps past Earth once per rotation.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Opacity, Optical Depth and Mean Free Path
concepts.topic: Opacity, Mean Free Path & Optical Depth
concepts.summary: Optical depth, the integral of kappa rho ds, counts the mean free paths a photon crosses, so the photosphere is by definition where that depth reaches 1 and the mean free path is 1/(kappa rho).

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Open versus Globular Clusters
concepts.summary: Open clusters are young, metal-rich disc systems of 10^2 to 10^3 stars, whereas globular clusters are ancient metal-poor haloes of 10^5 to 10^6 stars whose turnoffs sit below the solar mass.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Oppositions, Synodic Periods and Retrograde Loops
concepts.summary: A planet's synodic period with Earth follows 1/S = 1/P_planet - 1/P_Earth, giving 780 days for Mars, and the geometry of Earth catching up produces the opposition and its retrograde loop.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Parallax, Proper Motion and Precession
concepts.topic: Time Systems, Precession, Proper Motion & Parallax
concepts.summary: A parallax of p arcseconds puts a star at d = 1/p parsecs, proper motion is the transverse velocity divided by distance, and precession carries the equinoxes round the ecliptic once in about 26 000 years.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Phases of the Interstellar Medium
concepts.summary: The interstellar medium ranges from molecular clouds at 10 to 20 K and 10^2 to 10^6 particles per cm^3, through warm neutral gas near 8 000 K, to hot ionised gas above 10^6 K, the phases held in rough pressure balance.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Protostars, Accretion Discs and Outflows
concepts.summary: A collapsing core conserves angular momentum, so it flattens into a disc, drives bipolar outflows along the rotation axis, and reaches the main sequence only after a Kelvin-Helmholtz time of some 3x10^7 years at one solar mass.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Quantised Energy Levels and Ionisation
concepts.summary: A hydrogen electron occupies levels E_n = -13.6 eV / n^2, so 13.6 eV ionises the ground state and the n = 2 level lies 3.4 eV below the continuum.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Radiative Diffusion and Convection
concepts.summary: Radiative transport is a random walk that takes about 10^5 years to cross the solar interior, while convection takes over where the gradient exceeds the adiabatic one and carries the outer envelope in weeks to months.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Radii from Eclipse Durations and Velocities
concepts.summary: Eclipse durations divided by the projected orbital speed give the stellar radii directly, because ingress lasts exactly the time to cross one stellar diameter.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Red Giants and the Helium Flash
concepts.summary: Once core hydrogen is spent the core contracts and the envelope swells to 10 to 100 solar radii, and a one-solar-mass star ignites helium in a degenerate-core flash before settling onto the horizontal branch.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Refracting and Reflecting Telescope Designs
concepts.summary: Refractors suffer chromatic aberration and a size limit set by sagging glass, so every large telescope is a reflector, in Newtonian, Cassegrain or Ritchey-Chretien form according to the field and focal ratio required.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Rotational and Macroturbulent Broadening
concepts.summary: Rotation adds a profile whose full width is twice the projected equatorial speed, which is why a fast rotator shows broad shallow lines and a slow rotator narrow deep ones.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Seasons, Rise and Set, and Eclipse Geometry
concepts.summary: Seasons follow from the 23.4 degree tilt of Earth's axis rather than its varying distance from the Sun, and a solar eclipse needs a new moon within about 18 degrees of a lunar node.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Seeing, Adaptive Optics and Interferometry
concepts.summary: Atmospheric seeing near 1 arcsecond usually sets the real ground-based resolution, and interferometry beats both limits by combining apertures across a baseline B to reach roughly lambda/B.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: SI Units and Astronomical Distance Scales
concepts.summary: Every measurement reduces to the seven SI base units, and astronomy adds the astronomical unit (1.496x10^11 m), the light-year (9.46x10^15 m) and the parsec (3.086x10^16 m, or 3.26 ly).

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Sidereal and Solar Time
concepts.topic: Time Systems, Precession, Proper Motion & Parallax
concepts.summary: A sidereal day lasts 23 h 56 m 4 s of solar time because Earth must turn about one degree extra to bring the Sun back to the meridian, and that daily shortfall accumulates into the seasonal drift of the night sky.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Significant Figures and Propagated Uncertainty
concepts.summary: A quoted value carries only the digits the instrument resolves, so 12.30 mag claims 0.01 mag precision while 12.3 mag claims 0.1 mag, and averaging N readings shrinks random error as 1/sqrt(N) while a systematic offset survives.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Specific Intensity, Flux and Radiation Pressure
concepts.topic: The Radiation Field: Intensity, Flux & Radiation Pressure
concepts.summary: Specific intensity, the energy per area, time, solid angle and frequency, is conserved along a ray in vacuum, flux follows F = integral of I cos(theta) dOmega and falls as 1/d^2, and radiation pressure 4 sigma T^4/(3c) balances gravity at the Eddington luminosity.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Spectroscopic Parallax
concepts.summary: Spectral type plus luminosity class fixes absolute magnitude, and subtracting it from the apparent magnitude gives the distance through the distance modulus, with no geometric parallax needed.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Stellar Nucleosynthesis and Metallicity
concepts.summary: Fusion builds elements up to iron, elements beyond iron need neutron capture in AGB stars and supernovae, and each generation's ejecta raise the metallicity of the gas the next stars form from.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Structure and Rotation of the Milky Way
concepts.summary: The Galaxy is a barred spiral about 30 kpc across with the Sun 8 kpc from the centre, and its rotation curve stays near 220 km/s far beyond the visible disc, which implies a dark halo of several times the visible mass.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Temperature Ratio from Eclipse Depths
concepts.summary: The relative depths of the primary and secondary minima give the surface-brightness ratio, so the temperature ratio follows from the fourth root of the flux ratio in the same bandpass.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Boltzmann and Saha Equations
concepts.summary: The Boltzmann equation sets the level populations at (g2/g1) exp(-dE/kT) and the Saha equation sets the ionisation balance, which is why a cool star shows neutral lines and a hot star of the same element shows ionised ones.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The CMB and Its Acoustic Peaks
concepts.summary: The cosmic microwave background is a 2.725 K blackbody released at recombination near redshift 1 100, and its acoustic peaks fix a flat geometry and the baryon fraction.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Critical Density and Omega
concepts.topic: Scale Factor, Critical Density & the Fate of the Universe
concepts.summary: The critical density 3H0^2/(8 pi G) is about 9x10^-27 kg/m^3 for H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc, and the ratio Omega = rho/rho_c decides whether the spatial geometry is closed, flat or open.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Diffraction Limit
concepts.summary: A circular aperture resolves two points only when they are separated by more than 1.22 lambda/D radians, so a 0.1 m telescope at 500 nm is limited to about 1.3 arcseconds.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Distance Ladder and Its Systematics
concepts.summary: Parallax, Cepheids, the red-giant tip, the Tully-Fisher relation and Type Ia supernovae calibrate one another in sequence, so an error at one rung propagates into every distance above it.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Friedmann Equation and Accelerating Expansion
concepts.topic: Scale Factor, Critical Density & the Fate of the Universe
concepts.summary: The Friedmann equation ties the expansion rate to density and curvature, and the data since 1998 require a dark-energy density near 0.7, so the expansion accelerates instead of slowing.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Giant Planets and Their Interiors
concepts.summary: Jupiter and Saturn are 318 and 95 Earth masses of hydrogen and helium with metallic-hydrogen interiors, Uranus and Neptune are 14 to 17 Earth-mass ice giants, and all four lack a solid surface and carry strong magnetic fields.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Harvard Spectral Sequence
concepts.summary: The sequence OBAFGKM runs from about 50 000 K down to 2 500 K with ten subclasses each, so the Sun is a G2 star with T_eff near 5 800 K.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Hubble Sequence
concepts.summary: Galaxies divide into ellipticals, lenticulars, spirals and irregulars along the Hubble sequence, which orders them by the balance of bulge and disc rather than by a single evolutionary path.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Inverse-Square Law of Gravitation
concepts.summary: Two masses attract with F = G M m / r^2, so doubling the separation quarters the force and a satellite at twice Earth's radius weighs a quarter of what it does on the surface.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Jeans Mass and Gravitational Collapse
concepts.summary: A cloud collapses only when its mass exceeds the Jeans mass, which scales as T^(3/2) rho^(-1/2), so cold dense cores collapse while warm diffuse gas does not.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Main-Sequence Turnoff Age
concepts.summary: Because lifetime scales as M^(-2.5), a cluster's turnoff mass dates it, so the turnoff luminosity read from the colour-magnitude diagram is the cluster's clock.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Mass Function of a Single-Lined Binary
concepts.summary: A single-lined spectroscopic binary yields only the mass function (M2 sin i)^3/(M1 + M2)^2 = P K1^3/(2 pi G), so the companion mass stays a lower limit until the inclination is known.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Mass-Luminosity Relation
concepts.summary: Main-sequence stars obey L/L_sun near (M/M_sun)^3.5, so a ten-solar-mass star is about 3 000 times more luminous and, with only ten times the fuel, exhausts it roughly 300 times sooner.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The MK Luminosity Classes
concepts.summary: The Yerkes system appends Ia, Ib, II, III, IV or V to the spectral type and separates a supergiant from a dwarf of the same temperature, because a larger radius means lower gravity and narrower pressure-broadened lines.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Period-Density Relation for Pulsators
concepts.summary: A pulsating star obeys a constant product of period and the square root of mean density, so the period fixes that density and a Cepheid with a ten-day period has a radius of order 10^2 solar radii.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Pogson Magnitude Relation
concepts.summary: Five magnitudes correspond to a flux ratio of exactly 100, so m1 - m2 = -2.5 log10(F1/F2) and one magnitude is a factor of 2.512 in flux.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Proton-Proton Chain and the CNO Cycle
concepts.summary: Hydrogen fusion yields 26.7 MeV per helium nucleus, and the proton-proton chain dominates below about 1.3 solar masses while the far steeper CNO cycle takes over in more massive stars.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Protoplanetary Disc and Planetesimal Accretion
concepts.summary: A protoplanetary disc builds planetesimals from sticky grains and then cores by runaway accretion, and beyond the snow line near 3 au cores grow fast enough to capture hydrogen before the gas disperses in a few million years.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Radial-Velocity Method
concepts.summary: The stellar reflex motion has semi-amplitude proportional to m_p sin(i)/M_star times (2 pi G/P)^(1/3), so Jupiter moves the Sun by 12.5 m/s while Earth moves it by 9 cm/s.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Radiative Transfer Equation
concepts.topic: Radiative Transfer, the Gray Atmosphere & Line Formation
concepts.summary: Along a ray dI/ds = -kappa rho I + j, and in local thermodynamic equilibrium the source function equals the Planck function, so emergent intensity is B_nu averaged over the last unit of optical depth.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Rydberg Formula and Spectral Series
concepts.summary: Transitions obey 1/lambda = R(1/n_f^2 - 1/n_i^2) with R = 1.097x10^7 m^-1, placing the Balmer lines at 656, 486 and 434 nm and the Lyman series in the ultraviolet.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Schwarzschild Radius and Event Horizon
concepts.summary: The Schwarzschild radius 2GM/c^2 is 3 km per solar mass, so a ten-solar-mass black hole has a 30 km horizon and a clock hovering at twice that radius ticks at 1/sqrt(2) of the rate at infinity.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Spherical Law of Cosines
concepts.summary: The spherical law of cosines, cos a = cos b cos c + sin b sin c cos A, converts between horizon and equatorial coordinates once latitude, declination and hour angle are known.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Standard Solar Model
concepts.topic: The Sun as the Calibrating Standard Model
concepts.summary: A model with 1.989x10^30 kg, 6.96x10^8 m, 3.83x10^26 W and 5 772 K reproduces the observed p-mode frequencies and the 8.8 MeV boron-8 neutrino flux, which is how the interior solution is tested.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Stefan-Boltzmann Law
concepts.summary: A blackbody radiates F = sigma T^4 per unit area, so doubling T multiplies the output sixteenfold and a star's luminosity is L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Three Stellar Timescales
concepts.topic: Stellar Structure Equations, the Virial Theorem & Timescales
concepts.summary: The dynamical time sqrt(R^3/GM) is about 30 minutes for the Sun, the Kelvin-Helmholtz time about 3x10^7 years and the nuclear time about 10^10 years, which is why the Sun sits stably on the main sequence.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Transit Method
concepts.summary: A transiting planet dims its star by (R_p/R_star)^2, so a Jupiter across a Sun-like star gives a one per cent dip, and a hot Jupiter at 0.05 au repeats every four days.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Unified Model of Active Galactic Nuclei
concepts.summary: An active nucleus is powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole, and the viewing angle through the dusty torus explains why one engine appears as a Seyfert galaxy, a quasar or a blazar.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Virial Theorem
concepts.topic: Stellar Structure Equations, the Virial Theorem & Timescales
concepts.summary: For a bound, non-relativistic system 2K + Omega = 0, so half the energy released by contraction is radiated and half raises the internal temperature, which is why a collapsing cloud heats up.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: The Vis-Viva Equation and Orbital Energy
concepts.summary: The vis-viva equation v^2 = GM(2/r - 1/a) gives the speed anywhere on an orbit, and the sign of the specific energy -GM/2a separates bound, parabolic and hyperbolic paths.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Thermal and Pressure Broadening
concepts.summary: Thermal motion widens a line by delta lambda/lambda = sqrt(2kT/m)/c, about 4x10^-5 for hydrogen at 10 000 K, while collisions thicken the damping wings in proportion to density.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Tidal Forces, the Roche Limit and Lagrange Points
concepts.topic: Tides, the Roche Limit & Lagrange Points
concepts.summary: Tidal acceleration falls as 1/r^3, a fluid satellite is disrupted inside the Roche limit at about 2.44 R (rho_M/rho_m)^(1/3), and the five Lagrange points are where gravity and rotation balance in the co-rotating frame.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Total Mass from Kepler's Third Law
concepts.summary: For a visual binary the relative orbit gives a in astronomical units and P in years, so the total mass follows from M1 + M2 = a^3/P^2 in solar masses.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Wavelength, Frequency and the Spectrum
concepts.summary: All electromagnetic radiation obeys c = lambda nu, so the 21 cm hydrogen line sits at 1 420 MHz while a 1 m radio wave sits at 300 MHz, and the spectrum spans more than twenty orders of magnitude in frequency.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: White Dwarf Degeneracy and Cooling
concepts.summary: Electron degeneracy pressure holds a white dwarf near 0.01 solar radii only below the Chandrasekhar mass of 1.4 solar masses, and with no fusion source the star then cools along a sequence whose faint end dates its cluster.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe

concepts.title: Wien's Law and the Peak Wavelength
concepts.summary: A blackbody peaks at lambda_max = 2.898x10^-3 m K divided by T, so the Sun's 5 800 K photosphere peaks near 500 nm and a 300 K planet peaks in the thermal infrared near 10 microns.

provenance.source: Astrophysics - Tools, Stars, Galaxies and the Universe
